summary: Tested new Attendance & Payroll module (iteration 63). Backend: 9/10 pytest cases pass. Office admin + super admin flows work end-to-end (check-in, payroll math, salary edit, office scoping, payslip PDF download). CRITICAL bug: existing staff users cannot check in — their persisted `permissions` doc lacks the newly added `attendance` key, so `require_edit('attendance')` falls back to the staff default of 'none' and returns 403 'You have none-only access to attendance'. Frontend UI + role gating + testids are correct.

critical.issue: Staff role receives 403 'You have none-only access to attendance'. Root cause: STAFF_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS in models.py now includes attendance=edit, but pre-existing staff users in DB were seeded before this key was added. Their user.permissions dict is missing the `attendance` key, and auth_lib.require_edit defaults staff/user roles to 'none' when the key is missing. The default should either (a) fall back to STAFF_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS/OFFICE_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS map when a key is missing, or (b) seed.py must backfill `attendance:'edit'` on existing staff & office_admin permission maps on boot. Verified staff.blr@kmfoundation.online has permissions dict without an attendance key.

integration_issues.issue: Staff sees the Attendance nav item and Check-in card, clicks 'Check in' → backend returns 403 → toast 'You have none-only access to attendance'. Frontend perm.js defaults missing perms to 'edit' (so nav shows), but backend defaults to 'none' for staff → mismatch. Blocks the core staff usage. See backend critical bug above.

action_items: Fix permission mismatch for staff attendance: EITHER backfill user.permissions.attendance='edit' for all existing staff/office_admin rows in seed.py (idempotent), OR change auth_lib.require_edit to fall back to STAFF_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS/OFFICE_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS/USER_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS when a page key is missing from user.permissions, instead of the hard 'none' default for staff/user roles. Same issue will hit any future new PERMISSION_PAGES entry.
Consider aligning frontend perm.js `permFor` default (currently 'edit') with backend default so UI does not offer buttons that will 403; but the backend fix is the important one.
critical_code_review_comments: auth_lib.require_edit defaults missing permission keys to 'none' for staff/user roles — silently breaks every new PERMISSION_PAGES entry until users are re-seeded. Fragile; should read from *_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS map.
attendance.py _payroll_rows is O(users * attendance_rows); fine now but consider aggregation if attendance grows large.
attendance.py check-in stores lat/lng only from body; no server-side geofence check yet (per spec current). OK.

Frontend covered: office_admin sees both cards & scoped payroll (no office dropdown), super_admin sees payroll with office dropdown & no check-in card (nav is under 'Office' collapsible group), payslip PDF downloads OK, staff sees only check-in card but check-in is BROKEN due to backend perms bug. After main agent fixes permission fallback, re-run test_iteration63_attendance.py — the 3 currently-failing tests (test_staff_check_in_and_duplicate, test_staff_check_out, test_set_salary_and_payroll_math which also 403'd on /api/users listing — office admin can't list users via /api/users; that endpoint returns 403 for office_admin, unrelated to this module but worth noting) should pass once staff has attendance=edit.
rca of the issue: STEP 1 (reproduce): logged in as staff.blr@kmfoundation.online, POST /api/attendance/check-in → 403 body {"detail":"You have none-only access to attendance"}. STEP 2 (inspect DB): db.users.find_one(email='staff.blr…') returned permissions = {overview, quick_entry, transactions, accounts, clients, students, expense_requests, settings, leads, leave} — attendance key is ABSENT. STEP 3 (trace): auth_lib.require_edit line 152: `default_level = 'none' if role in ('user','staff') else 'edit'` → level='none' → 403. STEP 4 (why): iteration 63 added 'attendance' to models.STAFF_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS but did not migrate existing user rows; require_edit's staff default of 'none' means every newly-introduced page is 'none' by default for legacy staff rows. FIX (recommended): in require_edit, when perms.get(page) is None, look it up in the role's DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS map (STAFF_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS / OFFICE_ADMIN_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS / USER_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS) before falling back to 'none'. Alternative FIX: extend seed.py to $set permissions.attendance='edit' for role in ('staff','office_admin') and permissions.attendance='none' for role='user' if the key is missing. Frontend already uses 'edit' as the missing-key default so the UI is not visibly broken — only the API call fails.
